name: Pink Floyd
hook: A London underground band that recorded next door to the Beatles at Abbey Road, made one of the best-selling albums ever with a synthesizer sequence at its centre, and paid for Kate Bush's first proper demo.
blurb: Pink Floyd formed in London in 1965: Syd Barrett, Nick Mason, Roger Waters and Richard Wright. Their first leader, Barrett, wrote strange, playful songs, and the band played long, loud, experimental pieces with light shows in London's underground clubs; in 1966 and 1967 they were briefly a house band at the UFO Club, the centre of that scene. They signed to EMI on 15 February 1967 and recorded their first album, 'The Piper at the Gates of Dawn', with Norman Smith at Abbey Road between February and May, in the room next to the Beatles, who were making 'Sgt. Pepper'; on 21 March they watched the Beatles record 'Lovely Rita'. Barrett's mental health collapsed and David Gilmour replaced him in 1967. 'The Dark Side of the Moon' (March 1973), engineered by Alan Parsons, has sold more than 45 million copies. On one track, 'On the Run', a synthesizer, an EMS Synthi AKS, plays a fast eight-note pattern over and over, sped up on playback, an early sequenced synthesizer on a rock album sold to millions, years before that sound was common. Gilmour also paid for a 16-year-old Kate Bush to record a demo, which got her a deal with EMI. 'The Wall' (1979) was number one in America for fifteen weeks. Their last studio album was 'The Endless River' (2014). They have never formally split, and Gilmour and Mason recorded a single as Pink Floyd in 2022.
